title: Multi-Protocol Reference Architecture - Trust Layer for A2A + MCP Agent Ecosystems
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: peterzan/ILETP. Labels: help wanted, MCP, architecture, exploratory, rfc, A2A, ecosystem-integration, multi-protocol, trust-layer. # Issue: Multi-Protocol Reference Architecture - Trust Layer for A2A + MCP Agent Ecosystems

## Overview

Agent2Agent (A2A) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) are rapidly gaining enterprise adoption for agent coordination and tool access. However, both protocols lack built-in trust verification—a critical requirement for high-stakes deployments in healthcare, finance, legal, and other regulated industries. 

**ILETP provides the missing trust layer**, enabling enterprises to deploy A2A + MCP agent systems with confidence through ensemble verification, audit trails, and provenance tracking.

This issue proposes a **reference architecture** showing how all three protocols work together to create enterprise-ready, trustworthy multi-agent systems.

**Status:** Exploratory RFC / Reference Architecture  
**Dependencies:** Builds on Issue #1 (Headless Server), optionally on Issue #2 (MCP Server)  
**Priority:** Medium (ecosystem positioning and integration)

**Important Note**: This issue is provided for community members who fork the repository and wish to build implementations. Any work completed here will **not be merged back into this repository**—it's intended for independent forks and derivative projects. That said, if you build something based on this issue, please let me know! I'd love to see what the community creates and may link to notable implementations.

title: Table of contents sidebar never sticks, so its scroll cap just traps content
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: AlmaLinux/almalinux.org. Labels: good first issue. The TOC sidebar on `p`-type pages is styled to stick as you scroll, but it doesn't. It scrolls away with the page. The height cap that exists because it's supposed to stick is still active, so on shorter windows the TOC gets its own scrollbar and then scrolls off screen anyway.

**Cause.** The sticky rule is on the wrong element. From `layouts/p/single.html`:

```html
<aside class="col-lg-3 ...">         <!-- flex item, stretches to full row height -->
  <nav class="al-page-toc">          <!-- height: auto, sized to its content -->
    <div class="al-page-toc-inner">  <!-- position: sticky, top: 1rem -->
```

`main.scss:530` puts `position: sticky` on `.al-page-toc-inner`, but its containing block is `nav.al-page-toc`, which has no height rule (`main.scss:438` sets only `font-size`). The nav is exactly as tall as the inner div, so there's no room to travel and sticky does nothing. The `<aside>` does stretch to full row height, but that never reaches the sticky element.

The coupled rule at `main.scss:461-462`:

```scss
.al-page-toc #TableOfContents {
  max-height: calc(100vh - 8rem);
  overflow-y: auto;
}
```

The cap is only worth having if the sidebar sticks.

**Decide which we want:**

- **Keep floating.** Move `position: sticky` to `.al-page-toc`, or give `.al-page-toc` `height: 100%`. Keep the cap.
- **Drop it.** Remove the sticky rule and the `max-height`/`overflow-y` cap together. TOC becomes a plain block that scrolls with the page.

```html
title: Feature: Multi-hop document-RAG for cross-document questions
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: trustgraph-ai/trustgraph. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, size: large. ## Summary

Document-RAG currently performs a single retrieval pass: extract concepts → embed → fetch matching chunks → synthesise answer.  This works well when the answer lives in one or two chunks, but falls short for questions that span multiple documents or require connecting information across sections.

A multi-hop retrieval loop would let the LLM read initial chunks, identify what information is still missing, and issue follow-up queries — iterating until it has enough context to answer.

## Motivation

Example questions that need multi-hop:

- *"How does the data retention policy interact with the GDPR compliance requirements?"* — retention policy is in one document, GDPR requirements in another
- *"Compare the authentication mechanisms described in the v2 and v3 architecture documents"* — needs chunks from two different documents
- *"What are all the prerequisites for deploying the production pipeline?"* — prerequisites may be scattered across setup guide, infrastructure doc, and runbook

Today these queries retrieve chunks biased toward one aspect of the question and miss the rest.

## Proposed design

Please PR against the latest `release/vX.Y` branch.

### Iterative retrieval loop

```
1. Extract concepts from query (existing step)
2. Retrieve initial chunks (existing step)
3. Loop (max N iterations):
   a. Present query + retrieved chunks to LLM with a "reflection" prompt
   b. LLM outputs either:
      - SUFFICIENT: enough context to answer → break
      - FOLLOW_UP: one or more follow-up queries for missing info
   c. For each follow-up query: extract concepts → embed → retrieve chunks
   d. Deduplicate and append to chunk set
4. Synthesise answer from full chunk set (existing step)

This policy uses **boolean rules**: `default <name> := false` with a matching
`<name> if { ... }`. There are roughly **21** of them.

For each, write a case with input that makes it true, and one where it stays
false. Boolean rules are where the `{}` trap bites — a rule with no `default`

report object.

- [ ] Each rule has a case that exercises it

- [ ] The compliance report is asserted to be a **populated object on empty input**, not `{}`

description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: kubestellar/kubestellar. Labels: help wanted, lifecycle/stale, roadmap. ## Strategic Finding

**Type**: governance / hygiene
**Horizon**: near-term

Commit `2f354fab` (2026-06-08) in `kubestellar/console` cleaned up 5 agent-generated log files that were accidentally committed to `main`:

- `cron_scan_log.md`
- `release-failure-diagnosis.md`
- `release-failure-summary.txt`
- `pr.md`
- `reviewer_log.md`

These were added to `.gitignore` in the fix commit. However, this pattern is likely replicated across other hive-managed repos.

1. **Sensitive operational data in public git history** — agent logs can contain internal state, error messages, token-adjacent information

3. **Consider `git filter-repo`** to remove sensitive log history if warranted (requires maintainer review)

description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: NickGhignatti/crowd-vision. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, thinking, ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ hard. ## Description
This issue outlines a proposal to develop a passive wireless monitoring system designed to detect and analyze mobile devices within a defined physical perimeter. By capturing ambient wireless signals and analyzing telemetry metrics, the system will evaluate device density, spatial movement, and dwell times to generate actionable analytics regarding area occupancy and foot traffic.

## Goals
- Signal Capture: Passively intercept and log ambient wireless emissions (e.g., probe requests, broadcasting beacons, or discovery packets) within the operational range of designated hardware sensors.
- Proximity Estimation: Utilize signal strength metrics (such as Received Signal Strength Indicator, or RSSI) to approximate the distance, proximity, and spatial distribution of detected devices.
- Data Aggregation: Process the collected telemetry to produce accurate, high-level analytics detailing occupancy rates and generalized movement patterns.

## Considerations
- Regulatory Compliance and Privacy: The collection of persistent hardware identifiers constitutes the processing of Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Strict anonymization protocols—such as applying daily rotating cryptographic salts to device addresses—must be implemented to ensure full compliance with data protection frameworks (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) prior to any production deployment.
- Identifier Randomization: Modern mobile operating systems continuously cycle randomized hardware identifiers (such as MAC addresses) while broadcasting or scanning for networks. The engineering team must evaluate and integrate heuristic models to account for this rotation; failure to do so will result in artificially inflated unique-visitor metrics.

title: header row support in slice_csv
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: K-Kernel/Themis. Labels: enhancement, good first issue. ### Current behaviour
 
`slice_csv` treats every line of the input as a data row. `Table::header` is
always constructed empty, and there is no way to address a column by name.
 
The `bool has_header` parameter has been removed rather than left inert: it
previously accepted a value and did nothing, which is worse than its absence
because the signature promised behaviour that was not implemented.
 
### Expected behaviour
 
An opt-in way to tell the parser that the first record is a header. When set:
 
- the first record's fields populate `Table::header` instead of `Table::cells`
- `nrows()` counts data rows only, excluding the header
- columns become addressable by name, e.g. `col("carbon_kg")` returning the
  column index, or `std::nullopt` if absent
### Design questions to settle before implementing
 
- **Detection.** Explicit flag, or sniffing (first record is all non-numeric
  while later records are not)? Sniffing is convenient and occasionally wrong;
  an explicit flag is never wrong and always needs a caller decision. Possibly
  both, with sniffing only as the default when the caller expresses no opinion.
- **Column count disagreement.** When the header has a different field count
  from the body, which wins? Proposal: the header defines `ncols()`, and body
  rows are padded or truncated against it under the existing ragged-row policy.
- **Duplicate names.** `a,b,a` is legal CSV and common in exported data.
  Proposal: keep both, have `col()` return the first match, and record a
  `ParseError`.
- **Empty names.** A trailing delimiter in the header produces an unnamed
  column. It still exists and still needs an index.
- **Whitespace.** `id, name, age` has a leading space in two names. Trim
  header names, or preserve them exactly? Trimming makes lookup work the way

title: The no-model fallback has no route for [RuntimeProvided] types outside Primitives
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: eQuantic/equantic-ui. Labels: enhancement, good first issue, help wanted. When eqc runs **without a project semantic model** (the documented fallback, `SymbolsAreAuthoritative = false`), a type marked `[RuntimeProvided]` that lives outside `eQuantic.UI.Primitives` has no route to `@equantic/runtime`. The scanner that fills `ComponentDefinition.RuntimeProvidedTypes` needs symbols to see the attribute, and `ComponentDependencyResolver` (after #148) correctly stops registering such a class as a per-app static helper — so the name ends up in **no** set, and the emitter falls back to its last heuristic: `Type.Member` of an unknown type is read as an enum member.

**Measured** (#148, `RuntimeProvidedClassTests`, on top of `main` at 6a1af334): with

```csharp
[RuntimeProvided] public static class ButtonStyles { public const int MinWidth = 64; }
public class Probe { public int Build() => ButtonStyles.MinWidth; }
```

the fallback emits `return 'minWidth';` — a string literal, no import. Before #148's resolver skip the same probe emitted `import … from "./ButtonStyles"`, a module that no longer exists. Both are wrong answers; with symbols the import is `from "@equantic/runtime"`, which is the right one.

**Do**
- Let `ComponentDependencyResolver` record the top-level types it sees carrying `[RuntimeProvided]` (by syntax — that is all the fallback has) and expose them, e.g. `GetRuntimeProvidedTypes()`.

- Keep the semantic path untouched: with a model, `RuntimeProvidedTypeScanner` already answers.

title: [Bug] Internal smali assembler silently emits invalid DEX when `.catch` regions are nested/overlapping
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: REAndroid/APKEditor. Labels: bug, good first issue. **Describe the bug**
When rebuilding with `-dex-lib = internal` (the default), the smali assembler accepts nested (overlapping) `.catch` try-regions and emits the overlapping ranges verbatim as `try_item`s. The DEX spec requires try items within a `code_item` to be sorted, in-range and **non-overlapping** — so the produced dex is invalid.

Official smali (baksmali/smali, also used by apktool) supports nested `.catch` by flattening overlaps into disjoint try ranges with merged handler sets. APKEditor's internal assembler does neither: the build **succeeds with zero warnings** ("Saved to: …") and the invalid dex is shipped. On device, ART then refuses to open the whole dex file, so *every* class in that dex becomes unresolvable at runtime (`NoClassDefFoundError` on a perfectly valid, unrelated class). The `d` command happily disassembles such a file back — nothing in the toolchain ever complains.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Used version `APKEditor 1.4.9`, ARSCLib `1.3.9` **and** `1.4.0` (both affected), OpenJDK `26.0.1+8-34`, device Android 13
2. Operating system `Windows 11 x64`
3. Command — see attached `apkeditor-nestedcatch-repro.zip` (includes prebuilt `nested.apk` / `flat.apk` / `nested_jf.apk`):
```
build_repro.bat <path-to-apkeditor.jar>
```
It builds two ready-made mini projects (identical semantics, different catch layout) and validates the produced dexes with `dexcheck.py` (standalone, no deps):

* `mini_nested/` — one class, one method, outer `.catch` region fully containing an inner one (legal smali):

This is the single highest-leverage UX improvement available, and probably the best-loved command the project could ship. **A confidence score you cannot interrogate is a score nobody trusts** — and a system that influences repository governance must never behave like an unexplained scoring black box. It is also the best possible demo recording.

## Scope of change

**`checkowners explain PATH`:**

```text
path/to/file.py

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
@alice                        0.86 confidence
  Recency 0.92   Frequency 0.81   Blame 0.89   Reviews 0.74
  37 commits · 68% current blame · 11 reviews
  last meaningful change: 12 days ago

@bob                          0.54 confidence
  Recency 0.33   Frequency 0.58   Blame 0.62   Reviews 0.71

Evidence quality:             0.91
```

```text

- last contribution: 418 days ago
```

title: [P1] Persist JetBrains plugin settings across IDE restarts
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Sandesh13fr/TCalc. Labels: bug, help wanted, OSCI'26. ## Problem

The JetBrains plugin stores its configuration in an application service with mutable in-memory fields, but `WmaSettingsState` does not implement `PersistentStateComponent` and has no `@State`/`@Storage` declaration. Values entered under **Settings → Tools → TCalc** therefore return to defaults after the IDE restarts.

## Evidence

- `apps/jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/tcalc/plugin/settings/WmaSettingsState.kt` is only annotated with `@Service`.
- `WmaSettingsConfigurable.apply()` writes the Node path, CLI path, goal, privacy mode, and token budget only to that in-memory service.
- There is no persistence implementation or restart-level test in the plugin.

## Reproduction

1. Open Settings → Tools → TCalc.
2. Set a non-default CLI path, goal, or token budget and apply it.
3. Restart the IDE.
4. Reopen TCalc settings; the configured values are lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- Persist settings using the supported IntelliJ Platform state/storage APIs.
- Preserve all five current settings across IDE restarts.
- Keep defaults for a fresh installation and handle older/missing state safely.
- Add focused tests for state serialization/restoration or an equivalent persistence fixture.
- Document the manual restart verification and run the JetBrains plugin checks.

```csharp
public interface IBot
{
```

title: Add new fictional cases to the ledger (teaching and held-out)

Sixteen is small enough that a single case moves the headline numbers (facts-only 14/16, biological MaleCNS 13/16, shuffled 11/16). **What a contribution looks like**

- One or more new petitions in `apps/web/public/legalfly/cases.json`, following the existing schema: petitioner, title, petition text, the eight facts (matter, property, harm, proof, intent, relationship, urgency, ability), and the charter action.

- Keep the village early-modern and fictional. No real people, real jurisdictions, or real legal advice.
- Run `npm test` and `npm run test:legalfly` in `apps/web`; the ledger validation test must still pass.

**Things to know**

- Adding cases changes the teaching set, so the readout retrains in the browser on every "Teach the ledger". That is expected.
- If you change the held-out split, say so in the PR and report the new scores for all five systems in the results table so the README can be updated honestly.

title: Add keyboard navigation and ARIA labels to the board

Add keyboard navigation across board squares (arrow keys to move focus, Enter/Space to select/move) and appropriate ARIA roles/labels (e.g. `role="grid"`/`gridcell"`, `aria-label` describing each square's contents and coordinates) so the board is navigable and announced correctly by screen readers.

## Acceptance criteria
- The full board can be navigated and a legal move can be completed using only the keyboard.
- Screen readers announce square coordinates and piece presence/color/king status.
- Selected piece and legal destination squares are conveyed to assistive tech, not just via the `verde` CSS class.
- No regression to existing mouse/touch interaction.
